channel.title: Who Gives the Most AI Usage
channel.description: New articles and studies that measure and compare how much real usage AI subscriptions give: plan limits, API-equivalent value, and usage multipliers.

item.title: Adam Holter measures cost per task on subscription plans: on $20 plans, a dollar of GPT-6.1 Sol costs 7x a dollar of Opus, but a task only 1.3x
item.description:
Adam Holter ran a set of benchmarks on his subscription plans and priced each task in plan usage, not just API-equivalent dollars. His argument is that API-equivalent value alone isn't enough, because models differ a lot in how efficiently they use tokens.

  • On $20 plans, a dollar of GPT-6.1 Sol usage costs 7x what a dollar of Opus 5.5 does, but per finished task it's only about 1.3x.
  • Sonnet 5.5 costs 2.8x what Sol does per task on the API, but only about a third as much on $20 plans.
  • GPT-6 Luna costs half what Haiku 5.5 does per task on the API, but about 3x more on plans.
  • After OpenAI's Oct 29 limit doubling, he says it "completely changes the Pareto frontier" when resets are counted. Without resets, OpenAI is roughly in line with Claude. His live charts are on mypriors.com.

These numbers come from one person's benchmark runs, not a large sample of accounts.

item.title: Wokey's live dashboard measures 513 real subscription accounts: Claude plans return about 32 to 35 times their price at API rates, ChatGPT Plus about 12 times
item.description:
Wokey's coding plan comparison converts real subscription usage into API-equivalent dollars, using limit-meter changes on 513 accounts behind its gateway, and remeasures every Monday (latest data Oct 26). A full week of Claude Max 20x ($200/mo) was worth about $1,602 at API prices (35 times its price), Claude Pro ($20) about $157 (34 times), and ChatGPT Plus with Codex ($20) about $55 (12 times).

  • Max 20x gives about 10 times Pro's weekly limit; only the 5-hour window is near 20 times (about 24 times).
  • ChatGPT Plus (Codex) value fell from $92 a week on Oct 8 to $55 on Oct 26, which Wokey marks as a confirmed 58% drop.
  • Its real-traffic Max 20x figure (about $6,944 a month) sits below SemiAnalysis's single-model maximums, and it agrees with SemiAnalysis that vendors A/B-test limits.

ChatGPT Pro $200 is still collecting data (it needs 5 accounts). Note that Wokey sells pay-as-you-go access, and these are its own measured estimates, not vendor figures. Per-vendor pages: Claude Code vs Codex limits.

item.title: SemiAnalysis: Anthropic subscriptions offer 5x+ more value than OpenAI
item.description:
SemiAnalysis measured the limits on AI subscription plans from Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, SpaceXAI, Cursor, Cognition, and the Chinese labs, one token type at a time. It then converted each plan into what the same usage would cost at API prices.

For the mid-tier models, Claude plans gave about 5x the API-equivalent value of OpenAI's, after OpenAI halved its $200 plan and added a $500 tier. This is the founding example for this feed.
